From afa9a05e6c4971bd5586f1b304e14d61fb3d9385 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Yang Yang <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Date: Thu, 26 Mar 2026 03:44:41 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] vxlan: validate ND option lengths in vxlan_na_create

vxlan_na_create() walks ND options according to option-provided
lengths. A malformed option can make the parser advance beyond the
computed option span or use a too-short source LLADDR option payload.

Validate option lengths against the remaining NS option area before
advancing, and only read source LLADDR when the option is large enough
for an Ethernet address.

Fixes: 4b29dba9c085 ("vxlan: fix nonfunctional neigh_reduce()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Reported-by: Yifan Wu <yifanwucs@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Juefei Pu <tomapufckgml@gmail.com>
Tested-by: Ao Zhou <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Co-developed-by: Yuan Tan <tanyuan98@outlook.com>
Signed-off-by: Yuan Tan <tanyuan98@outlook.com>
Suggested-by: Xin Liu <bird@lzu.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Yang Yang <n05ec@lzu.edu.cn>
Reviewed-by: Ido Schimmel <idosch@nvidia.com>
Acked-by: Nikolay Aleksandrov <razor@blackwall.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260326034441.2037420-4-n05ec@lzu.edu.cn
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/vxlan/vxlan_core.c b/drivers/net/vxlan/vxlan_core.c
index 17c941aac32d..a94ac82a6136 100644
--- a/drivers/net/vxlan/vxlan_core.c
+++ b/drivers/net/vxlan/vxlan_core.c
@@ -1965,12 +1965,14 @@ static struct sk_buff *vxlan_na_create(struct sk_buff *request,
 	ns_olen = request->len - skb_network_offset(request) -
 		sizeof(struct ipv6hdr) - sizeof(*ns);
 	for (i = 0; i < ns_olen-1; i += (ns->opt[i+1]<<3)) {
-		if (!ns->opt[i + 1]) {
+		if (!ns->opt[i + 1] || i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) > ns_olen) {
 			kfree_skb(reply);
 			return NULL;
 		}
 		if (ns->opt[i] == ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR) {
-			daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr);
+			if ((ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) >=
+			    sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN)
+				daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr);
 			break;
 		}
 	}
-- 
2.34.1

The patch modifies one file, `drivers/net/vxlan/vxlan_core.c`, to add two bounds-checking validations in the function `vxlan_na_create()`:

1. In the loop that iterates over ND options, a new condition `|| i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) > ns_olen` is added to the existing zero-length check. This prevents the parser from advancing beyond the total ND option area when a malformed option specifies an incorrect length.

2. When a `ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR` option is found, the patch ensures that the option is large enough to contain the header plus an Ethernet address (`ETH_ALEN`) before reading the source link-layer address. This prevents reading a too-short option payload.

**Relationships between modifications:**  
Both changes address the same underlying issue – malformed ND options that could cause out-of-bounds memory access or incorrect parsing. The first check guards the overall loop bounds (option offset vs. total length), while the second check protects a specific read operation within the loop. Together, they ensure that every option’s claimed length is validated before any data is read from it.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>for (i = 0; i < ns_olen-1; i += (ns->opt[i+1]<<3))</text>
<text>if (!ns->opt[i + 1]) { kfree_skb(reply); return NULL; }</text>
<text>daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr);</text>
Reason:
The loop uses the option-provided length (`ns->opt[i+1]<<3`) to advance through the ND option area, but only validates that the length is non‑zero. It does not check whether the computed next offset remains within the total ND option length (`ns_olen`). This allows a malformed option with a length that causes `i` to exceed `ns_olen`, leading to an out‑of‑bounds read. Additionally, when the option type is `ND_OPT_SOURCE_LL_ADDR`, `daddr` is assigned without verifying that the option is large enough to contain an Ethernet address (`ETH_ALEN`), which can result in reading a too‑short payload or beyond the option boundary.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>if (!ns->opt[i + 1] || i + (ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) > ns_olen) { kfree_skb(reply); return NULL; }</text>
<text>if ((ns->opt[i + 1] << 3) >= sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN)
				daddr = ns->opt + i + sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr);</text>
Reason:
The first fix adds a check that the option length (shifted by 3) plus the current index `i` does not exceed `ns_olen`. This ensures the parser stays within the allocated ND option area, preventing both out‑of‑bounds reads and a premature loop exit caused by a malformed length. The second fix only reads the source LLADDR payload when the option is at least `sizeof(struct nd_opt_hdr) + ETH_ALEN` bytes long, guaranteeing that a full Ethernet address can be safely extracted and avoiding reads beyond the option’s actual data.
